name: Sketching: commit the camera at minute 5

script.doThis: Underline whose POV, who is present, the moment or emotion, and the medium limits (HB only, given space). Copy the 4 criteria into the margin.
Two thumbnails (≈5 cm) with different eye heights or framings. Fix eye height first: a chair seat ≈ 45 cm gives a low horizon with adults looming; a ceiling camera is a plan view.
Pick one thumbnail against the gate. Mark the horizon and vanishing points on the final sheet.

5–8 block: ground plane, gesture figures in fore, middle and back, one in-frame POV cue (chair leg, snout, lamp rim). 8–18 line: heavy near, light far; most time on the faces and body language the brief names; add setting props. 18–21 tone: depth and ground shadows only.
Is the POV unmistakable? Every named character and action present? Inside the given space?

failureModes: Drawing from a normal standing eye level: the brief's POV is lost
Tiny figures with faces too small to read an expression
Over-shading or rendering instead of finishing the whole scene
Drawing only part of the "whole scene" asked for
Hesitant, hairy lines and wrong proportions

name: Creativity: generate readings, then commit to the twist
decision: Which symbol readings make a story with a frame-4 twist

script.doThis: Write the hard rules in shorthand: symbols per frame, each used once, rotate/flip/scale only, title, frames numbered 1–4. Breaking one is the cheapest way to lose marks.

3+ literal and non-literal readings per symbol (circle → sun, coin, plate, porthole, eye). Pair readings into candidate worlds. Keep generating to the bell: ideas do not run out as early as they feel.
Pick the pairing with a frame-4 reversal (setup, build, turn, punchline) that passes the gate. Assign symbols to frames. Draft the title.
One consistent character, one action per frame, varied shot distance (wide, medium, close). Simple figures; symbols drawn unmodified and recognisable.
Title present, frames numbered, each symbol used exactly once and still readable, light hatching for clarity.

failureModes: First-reading cliché (sun drawn as a sun)
No ending turn: the story just stops
Symbols distorted, reused or missing
Character changes look between frames
Frames overcrowded with detail

name: Visual sensitivity: write the system rules before drawing

script.doThis: Note the set members, audience, colour limit, text ban and box size.
3 metaphors per subject (Ocean Science → wave, submarine, coral, conch). Keep the least generic one that still reads instantly; add an Indian cue where the audience asks for it.

Write the rules: container shape, grid, single stroke weight or fill-vs-outline, corner radius, flat front view, one shared motif. For lettering: list the given letters' stroke contrast, terminals and ornament.
Draw all items in parallel, stage by stage (container → main shape → detail), so none is left unfinished. Keep detail low enough to read small.
Squint test: equal visual weight across the set. No text crept in? Every item finished?

failureModes: Mixed styles: one outline, one filled, one 3D
Illustrations instead of icons
Text creeping into a no-text brief
Last item rushed or unfinished

name: Form sensitivity: run the operation matrix, then commit
decision: Which transformation of the given form

script.doThis: Note the function, the given form, the allowed operations (cut, add, subtract, deform, repeat) and that its essence must stay.

5–8 thumbnails, about one per operation: cut → shell seat; subtract → scooped cavity; repeat → cluster; deform → squashed pouf; add → form on segment legs. Keep the source form readable in silhouette.
Gate plus a usability check: right height (seat ≈ 40–45 cm), a back or lean surface, stable, clear how it is used.
11–20: one large 3/4 hero view, one light source, material by tone, cast shadow. 20–22: side view or detail callout, human silhouette for scale, material labels, one-line form → function rationale.
Light direction consistent? Essence of the form still obvious? Labels legible?

failureModes: Generic product with the form stuck on: essence not used
Form kept intact so it is not usable (a sphere that rolls)
All the time spent rendering one weak idea
Inconsistent light direction

name: Problem identification: budget problem finding, then commit twice
decision: Four problems of different types, then the one with two distinct solution directions

script.doThis: Note the deliverable split and marks (2026: 8 for four HMWs, 12 for two solutions). The time split follows the marks.

Framing: walk the journey or scene step by step. At each step apply lenses: user (age, mobility, language), activity (luggage, toilets, medicines, payment), environment (climate, crowds, steps), other stakeholders. Dump 10–15 raw problems as keywords.
Pick 4 that differ in type (physical, informational, social, safety) and stage. Phrase each as "How can we [verb] [for whom] [in what context]".
Pick the one HMW with two clearly different directions (e.g. product vs service).
Each solution in its box: sketch it in use with the user and context, 2–4 arrow notes, a short title. The two must differ in principle, not just in form.
Titles present? Every statement starts with "How can we"? Feasible at Indian cost levels?

failureModes: Five versions of one problem type
Vague statements ("make travel easier")
Tech-magic solutions: an app or robot for everything
Over-drawn scene that leaves no time for annotation
Solving more than the one HMW asked for
criteria: Variety and uniqueness of the problems
Practical feasibility of the design solutions
